html:
Sher Shah Suri was an Afghan soldier who drove the Mughal emperor Humayun out of India and ruled the north as sultan from 1540 to 1545, founding the Sur Empire. In five years he built a system of government that the Mughals later took over.

Born Farid Khan, son of a minor Afghan landholder at Sasaram in Bihar, he got the name Sher Khan, "tiger lord", supposedly for killing a tiger. He rose in the service of Afghan rulers in Bihar while Babur was founding the Mughal Empire. He took Bengal in 1538, beat Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and at Kannauj in 1540, and Humayun fled to Persia.

His reforms:

  • a survey of farmland and a fixed land revenue paid in cash;
  • a silver coin of standard weight, the rupiya, ancestor of the rupee;
  • the rebuilding of the Grand Trunk Road from Bengal to the Indus, with rest houses and post stations along it.

He was killed in 1545 when a store of gunpowder exploded during his siege of the fort of Kalinjar, and was buried in a great tomb at Sasaram. His successors quarrelled, and Humayun returned in 1555. Akbar built much of his empire on Sher Shah's revenue and coinage.
sum: Sher Shah Suri was an Afghan soldier who drove the Mughal emperor Humayun out of India and ruled the north as sultan from 1540 to 1545, founding the Sur Empire. In five years he built a system of government that the Mughals later took over.
